```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

This vignette demonstrates how to use the parser `form_4` to parse form 4 SEC
filings for insider trading information. We will be demonstrating the
following:

* Basic shape of the data, and an explaination of the variables.
* How to use the data to understand the management and director structure of a firm.

# Basic usage

```{r setup}
#library(secfilings)
devtools::load_all('.')
suppressMessages({
    library(dplyr)
})

tmpdir <- tempdir()
```

First we need to get the cik number for our symbol. Make sure to set the
useragent to your email address.

```{r get_cik}
useragent <- "Useragent useragent@example.com"
cik <- get_cik('TFC', useragent, cache=tmpdir)
```

Next we need to download all submissions associated with this cik and filter
based on form 4 and one year of data. I will be using the date `"2026-09-08"`
as the start. The output of the filter is a vector of accession numbers. This
vector is used to retrieve the filings from the SEC's EDGAR database. The final
output of this process is `filings`, which is a vector of paths to the
downloaded SGML files.

```{r get_submissions, message=FALSE}
submissions <- get_submissions(cik, useragent, cache=tmpdir)
accessions <- submissions |>
    filter(
        form == "4",
        reportDate < "2026-09-08" & reportDate > "2025-09-08") |>
    pull(accessionNumber)
filings <- get_filing(cik, accessions, useragent, cache=tmpdir)
```

We iterate over each file in `filings`, using the base package's `Filter`,
`Negate`, and `lapply` functions. If `form_4` returns `NULL`, which can happen
if the filing in not a Form 4, or if the Form 4 is older than 2003. We can
inspect one of the elements in the list and find the names of the tables, and
the number of forms that were successfully parsed.

```{r parse_list}
parsed <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(filings, parse_4))
names(parsed[[1]])
length(parsed)
```

We can combine the tables in each element by name and generate the full data
frames. These data frames are: `filing_all`, `owners_all`,
`nonderiv_transactions`, `nonderiv_holdings`, `deriv_transactions`,
`deriv_holdings`.

```{r build_tables}
filing_all            <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "filing"))
owners_all            <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "owners"))
nonderiv_transactions <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "nonderiv_transactions"))
nonderiv_holdings     <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "nonderiv_holdings"))
deriv_transactions    <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "deriv_transactions"))
deriv_holdings        <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "deriv_holdings"))
footnotes_all         <- bind_rows(lapply(parsed, `[[`, "footnotes"))
```

# The insider trading tables

We will now inspect each of the tables that were built in the previous step.

## The `filing` table

The filing table represents the metadata for the insider trading.

| variable | description |
|---:|:---|
| `accession` | The filing `accessionNumber` used to uniquely identify each filing. |
| `filedDate` | The date the form was filed with the SEC. |
| `schemaVersion` | The XML schema version (can be used to determine logical variables). |
| `documentType` | Should always be "4" for Form 4. |
| `periodOfRecord` | The snapshot date this information should be considered accurate. |
| `dateOfOriginalSubmissions` | Used if this is an ammended form 4 submission. |
| `issuerCik` | The cik number of the firm. |
| `issuerName` | The name of the firm, as registered with the SEC. |
| `issuerTradingSymbol` | The trading symbol used on stock exchanges. |
| `notSubjectToSection16` | Not relevant. |
| `aff10b5One` | Was this transaction executed under 10b5-1(c) pre-planned trading arrangement. |
| `remarks` | Any remarks. Should usually be null. |
| `signatureDate` | Should be the same as `filedDate`. |

```{r filing}
filing_all |> print(n = 5)

filing_all |> select(
        dateOfOriginalSubmission, issuerCik, issuerName, issuerTradingSymbol) |>
    print(n = 5)

filing_all |> select(
        notSubjectToSection16, aff10b5One, remarks, signatureName)
```

## The `owners` table

The owners table prints information about the owner. This information is useful
in constructing the relationship of the security owner and the firm.

| variable | description |
|---:|:---|
| `accession` | The filing `accessionNumber` used to uniquely identify each filing. |
| `rptOwnerCik` | A unique cik number to identify the security owner to the SEC. |
| `rptOwnerName` | The name of the security owner. |
| `isDirector` | A logical that determines if the security owner is a member of the board. |
| `isOfficer` | A logical that determines if the security owner is part of the senior management team. |
| `isTenPercentOwner` | A logical that indicates whether the security owner owns more than 10% of the outstanding shares in the firm. |
| `isOther` | A logical that  is a catch all. |
| `officerTitle` | If the security owner is part of the senior management team, what is their title. |

```{r owners}
owners_all |> print(n = 5)

owners_all |> select(isOther, officerTitle) |> print(n = 5)
```

## Nonderivative transactions

Non-deriviative usually means common stock. The first table tabluates the
security owners' transaction. A form 4 is usually filed when a significant
security owner buys or sells the security. There may be more than one
transaction per filed form.

| variable | description |
|---:|:---|
| `accession` | The filing `accessionNumber` used to uniquely identify each filing. |
| `securityTitle` | The type of security. Usually `Common Stock`. |
| `transactionDate` | The date the transaction was executed. |
| `deemedExecutionDate` | This applies under an employee benefit plan where the insider directs the plan to execute the trade. |
| `transactionCode` | Single letter symbol used to report the type of transaction (see below). |
|`equitySwapInvolved` | The transaction was an equity swap or similar hedging instrument. |
| `shares` | The number of shares transacted. |
| `pricePerShare` | The price per share the transaction was executed at. |
| `acquiredDisposedCode` | A single symbol determining whether shares were acquired (A) or disposed (D). |
| `sharesOwnedFollowing` | The number of shares the security owner owns after the transaction. |
| `ownershipType` | Whether the sares transacted were owned directly (D) or indirectly (I). |
| `natureOfOwnership` | How the transacter shares were acquired. See below. |
| `footnoteIds` | Relevant footnotes regarding this transaction which can be referenced in the footnotes table. |

### `transactionCode`

This variables identifies the SEC transaction code associated with this transaction. Possible values are:

| code | description |
|---:|:---|
| P | Open-market private purchase of secuity outside of the firm. |
| S | Open-market private sale of security outside of the firm. |
| A | A grant or award of shares from the company based on some criteria. |
| M | Exercise or conversion of a derivative security or stock option. |
| F | Payment of excise price or tax obligation. This is automatic based on taxes or fees. |
| G | A gift of stocks given or received.
| J | Other acquisition or disposal requiring a footnote explaination. |

### `natureOfOwnership`

This variable determines how the shares are owned and are free form. Possible values include: `By IRA`, `By Deferred Compensation`, `By Spouse`, etc...


```{r nonderiv_transactions}
nonderiv_transactions |> print(n = 5)

nonderiv_transactions |> select(
        equitySwapInvolved, shares, pricePerShare, acquiredDisposedCode) |>
    print(n = 5)

nonderiv_transactions |> select(
        sharesOwnedFollowing, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, footnoteIds) |>
    print(n = 5)
```

## Nonderivative holdings

The nonderivative holdings table specifies the holding of the security owner at
the time the form was filed with the SEC. Like the transaction table there may
be multiple instances per filing based on the nature of the ownership. I will
refer to different `natureOfOwnership`s as `buckets` because they are different
based on the nature of ownership. The instances in this table are the `buckets`
that are not transacted.

| variable | description |
|---:|:---|
| `accession` | The filing `accessionNumber` used to uniquely identify each filing. |
| `securityTitle` | The type of security. Usually `Common Stock`. |
| `sharesOwnedFollowing` | The number of shares owned in this bucket. |
| `ownershipType` | Direct (D) or indirect (I) |
| `natureOfOwnership` | please see `natureOfOwnership` above. |

You can notice in the holdings table below that there are more values for the
`natureOfOwnership`. This can give you a better idea of the range of values you
can get with this variable than the transaction table can.

```{r nonderiv_holdings}
nonderiv_holdings |> print(n = 5)
```

## Derivative transactions and holdings tables

Derivatives have a similar structure to the nonderiviatives tables. Typical
derivatives are Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), Options, etc... Most of the
instances in this table will represent vested items or stock options.

```{r deriv_transactions}
deriv_transactions |> print(n = 5)

deriv_holdings |> print(n = 5)
```

## Footnotes table

The footnotes table holds the footnotes that are associated with the
transactions. These are generally associated with the nonderivative
transactions only.

| variable | description |
|---:|:---|
| `accession` | The filing `accessionNumber` used to uniquely identify each filing. |
| `footnoteId` | The footnote id used to associate with the transaction. |
| `text` | The actual footnote text. |

```{r footnotes}
footnotes_all |> print(n = 5)
```

# An insider trading transaction history table

First table we will create is a structured history of insider trading. You can
usually find this type of table on other sites that show insider trading. We
create this table by combining the derivative and nonderivative transaction
tables and then associating the combined table with the owner via `accession`.
Using some manipulations, I created some standard columns and values.

```{r structured_transaction_history}
tx_history <- bind_rows(
        nonderiv_transactions |> mutate(class = "Non-Derivative"),
        deriv_transactions    |> mutate(class = "Derivative")) |>
    left_join(
        owners_all, by = "accession") |>
    transmute(
           Name = rptOwnerName,
           Role = case_when(
                isDirector ~ "Director",
                isOfficer  ~ officerTitle,
                .default   = "Neither"),
           Date = transactionDate,
           Shares = shares,
           Price = case_when(
                transactionCode == 'A' ~ "Award",
                transactionCode == 'M' ~ "Option",
                .default = paste0("$", as.character(pricePerShare))),
           Type = case_when(
                transactionCode == 'A' ~ "Award",
                transactionCode == 'P' ~ "Purchase",
                transactionCode == 'S' ~ "Sale",
                transactionCode == 'M' ~ "Exercise",
                transactionCode == 'F' ~ "Tax/Fees",
                transactionCode == 'G' ~ "Gift",
                transactionCode == 'F' ~ "Other"),
           `Shares Owned` = sharesOwnedFollowing)

tx_history |> print(n = 5)
```

# Per-filing totals

If we just wanted a running tally of the current ownership totals:

```{r current_ownership}
tx_bucket_latest <- nonderiv_transactions |>
    filter(securityTitle == "Common Stock") |>
    group_by(accession, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership) |>
    arrange(transactionDate, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(accession, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, sharesOwnedFollowing)

holdings_bucket_latest <- nonderiv_holdings |>
    filter(securityTitle == "Common Stock") |>
    distinct(accession, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(accession, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, sharesOwnedFollowing)

per_filing_totals <- bind_rows(tx_bucket_latest, holdings_bucket_latest) |>
    distinct(accession, ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    group_by(accession) |>
    summarize(filingCommonShares = sum(sharesOwnedFollowing, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    left_join(filing_all |> select(accession, periodOfReport), by = "accession") |>
    left_join(owners_all |> select(accession, rptOwnerCik, rptOwnerName),
              by = "accession")

per_filing_totals |>
    group_by(rptOwnerCik) |>
    filter(periodOfReport == max(periodOfReport)) |>
    summarize(rptOwnerName = first(rptOwnerName),
              totalCommonShares = first(filingCommonShares),
              asOf = first(periodOfReport),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    transmute(
        Name = rptOwnerName,
        `Total Shares` = totalCommonShares,
        `As Of` = asOf) |>
    arrange(desc(`As Of`)) |>
    print(n = 5)
```

# A breakdown of each security owners holdings

Using the `ownershipType` and `natureOfOwnership` we can further understand
each security owner's breakdown of ownership.

```{r bucket_breakdown}
bucket_breakdown <- function(target_accession) {
    tx <- nonderiv_transactions |>
        filter(accession == target_accession,
               securityTitle == "Common Stock") |>
        group_by(ownershipType, natureOfOwnership) |>
        arrange(transactionDate, .by_group = TRUE) |>
        slice_tail(n = 1) |>
        ungroup() |>
        select(ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, sharesOwnedFollowing)
    
    hold <- nonderiv_holdings |>
        filter(accession == target_accession,
               securityTitle == "Common Stock") |>
        select(ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, sharesOwnedFollowing)
    
    bind_rows(tx, hold) |>
        distinct(ownershipType, natureOfOwnership, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
        mutate(bucket = if_else(ownershipType == "D", "Direct",
                                paste0("Indirect - ", natureOfOwnership)))
}

# Helper: find a given owner's most recent accession, to feed into bucket breakdown()
latest_accession_for <- function(cik) {
    owners_all |>
        filter(rptOwnerCik == cik) |>
        left_join(filing_all |> select(accession, periodOfReport),
                  by = "accession") |>
        filter(periodOfReport == max(periodOfReport)) |>
        pull(accession)
}

cik <- owners_all$rptOwnerCik[2]
name <- owners_all$rptOwnerName[2]

breakdown <- bucket_breakdown(latest_accession_for(cik))

cat("For Owner: ", name)
cat("Direct: ", sum(breakdown$sharesOwnedFollowing[breakdown$ownershipType == "D"]))
cat("Indirect: ", sum(breakdown$sharesOwnedFollowing))
```

A management structure can also be regreated using form4s. Here we can get a
breakdown of who fills what senior management positions, as well as the
directors of the company. Note, like other listings, this information may
become stale. The `asOf` date is a signal to the freshness of the information.
If you see two people with the same title, the `asOf` date can be used to
distinguish the most current holder of that position.

```{r senior_management}
owners_all |>
    left_join(filing_all |> select(accession, periodOfReport),
              by = "accession") |>
    group_by(rptOwnerCik) |>
    filter(periodOfReport == max(periodOfReport)) |>
    summarize(
        rptOwnerName = first(rptOwnerName),
        isDirector   = first(isDirector),
        isOfficer    = first(isOfficer),
        officerTitle = first(officerTitle),
        asOf         = first(periodOfReport),
        .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(role = case_when(
        isOfficer & isDirector ~ "Officer & Director",
        isOfficer              ~ "Officer",
        isDirector             ~ "Director",
        TRUE                   ~ "Other (10% owner)")) |>
    arrange(desc(isOfficer), desc(asOf))
```

Finally, you can get a list of all of the insider traders, the `monthStale`
variable can be used to signal that someone potentially left the company or the
directorship.

```{r stale_signal}
owners_all |>
    left_join(filing_all |> select(accession, periodOfReport), by = "accession") |>
    group_by(rptOwnerCik) |>
    filter(periodOfReport == max(periodOfReport)) |>
    summarize(
        rptOwnerName = first(rptOwnerName),
        isDirector   = first(isDirector),
        isOfficer    = first(isOfficer),
        officerTitle = first(officerTitle),
        lastFiling   = first(periodOfReport),
        .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
        monthsStale = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.Date(), lastFiling, units = "days")) / 30.44,
        flag = case_when(
            monthsStale > 18 ~ "STALE - verify current status",
            monthsStale > 12 ~ "aging - watch",
            TRUE             ~ "current")) |>
        arrange(desc(monthsStale))
```
